This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Buckley Space Force Base Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 1 Jun '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Buckley Space Force Base Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/us/co/aurora/KBKF.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: National Weather Service forecasts for Denver project a high in the low 80s Fahrenheit on June 1, well above the 76°F threshold that commands 95% market-implied odds. This positioning reflects the typical early-summer warming pattern after Denver’s warmest spring in over a decade, with current model consensus showing minimal cooling influence from any passing systems. Official point forecast matrices indicate daytime maxima around 82°F under mostly clear conditions, consistent with climatological averages for early June. While short-term model runs remain subject to minor adjustments from evolving upper-level patterns, a significant downward revision sufficient to drop the high below 76°F would require an unexpected surge of cooler air not currently indicated in guidance.
